case_name: Virender Prasad Singh v Rajesh Bhardwaj & Ors.
facts: The concerned criminal case was initiated by a First Information Report registered on 6.12.2007.

It is an admitted position that the investigation had been completed and the police was going to submit the charge sheet dated 18.6.2009, but before that, the mother of the respondent No.1/accused filed Crl. WJC No.394 of 2009 before the High Court.

The First Information Report refers to the incident which took place on 30.11.2007, according to which at 10 p.m. on that day, the accused went to the house of the deceased Sonu, the daughter of the appellant/complainant and left with the deceased on his motorcycle in presence of the witnesses.
The Railway Police registered the case as GRP Case No.73 of 2007 for offences punishable under Sections 364, 302, 201 and 120B IPC.

An application for orders u/s.438 of the Criminal Procedure Code (Cr.P.C.) was moved by the respondent No.1/accused before the Sessions Court, Arrah, which was dismissed by the Court vide order dated 18.3.2008.
The respondent No.1/accused did not stop there and moved to this Court by way of a Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.5140 of 2008.

On 6.4.2009, one more petition came to be filed before the High Court being Cr. WJC No.352 of 2008, wherein the High Court was pleased to direct the Magistrate to dispose of the objection petition filed by the complainant after hearing both the parties and it was directed that till then the issuance of process of attachment u/s.83 Cr.P.C. would remain stayed.
On 15.5.2009, another petition being Crl. WJC No.394 of 2009 came to be filed before the High Court by the mother of the accused.

On 18.6.2009, police came to the conclusion that the offences alleged against the accused were committed by him and, therefore, the charge sheet came to be filed for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 201 and 120B IPC.
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in issuing directions for re-examination of the completed investigation by an officer of the rank of Director General of Police (DGP).
Whether the respondent No.1/accused has a right to anticipatory bail.

Whether the investigation was being influenced from the complainant's side and there was a need for direction to the State Government to get the case investigated by an independent investigating agency such as Central Bureau of Investigation.
petitioner_arguments: The appellant/complainant Virender Prasad Singh argued that the High Court has issued certain directions, whereby he has directed the re-examination of the completed investigation by an officer of the rank of Director General of Police (DGP).
He also argued that the respondent No.1/accused has not been arrested nor did he ever bother to appear before the Magistrate.
respondent_arguments: The respondent No.1/accused Rajesh Bhardwaj argued that his father's kidney had failed and that he was going to donate the kidney and he should be granted provisional anticipatory bail.
He also argued that the charge sheet was filed only for the offences punishable u/s.306 IPC and not under Sections 302, 201 and 120B IPC.
court_reasoning: The Court observed that this Court requests Mr. Manoj Nath to examine all the records of the case in detail and submit his report to this Court preferably within a period of one month with his clear opinion as to (i) whether investigation of the case is complete from all angles and case is fit to be tried on the basis of materials and report placed on record by the Investigating Officer only or (ii) whether there are some loopholes and lacunae in the investigation which necessitates further or fresh investigation of the case and if necessary by a more experienced and specialized agency, and/or (iii) what further steps, if any, are required to be taken in the case in the ends of justice, so that the guilty may not escape and the innocent may not suffer due to laches on the part of officers of the State.
holding: The Court granted leave and directed the re-examination of the completed investigation by an officer of the rank of Director General of Police (DGP).
The Court also observed that the respondent No.1/accused was still not arrested nor did he ever bother to appear before the Magistrate.
